gloss: scar; mark left by a wound

definitions.gloss: scar; mark left by a wound or injury
definitions.explanation: A physical mark remaining on the skin or a surface after a wound has healed. Also used figuratively for lasting emotional damage or evidence of past destruction.

examples.japanese: {腕|うで}に{傷跡|きずあと}が{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: There is a scar on my arm.

examples.japanese: {手術|しゅじゅつ}の{傷跡|きずあと}はだんだん{目立|めだ}たなくなった。
examples.english: The surgical scar gradually became less noticeable.

examples.japanese: {戦争|せんそう}の{傷跡|きずあと}は{今|いま}も{街|まち}のあちこちに{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: The scars of war still remain throughout the city.

notes:
{傷跡|きずあと} is a compound of {傷|きず} (wound) and {跡|あと} (trace, mark). It refers to the mark left after healing, not the wound itself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {傷跡|きずあと}が{残|のこ}る (a scar remains)
- {傷跡|きずあと}が{消|き}える (a scar fades)
- {傷跡|きずあと}が{目立|めだ}つ (a scar is noticeable)
- {心|こころ}の{傷跡|きずあと} (emotional scars)

USAGE NOTES:
The figurative usage is very common. {戦争|せんそう}の{傷跡|きずあと} (scars of war), {災害|さいがい}の{傷跡|きずあと} (scars of a disaster), and {心|こころ}の{傷跡|きずあと} (emotional scars) are all frequently seen in news and literature.
